approachQuestion.prompt: Reverse a supplied stack of n fixed-size integers, 0 <= n <= 2,000, in place. Only top push, top pop and empty checks may access it. Do not use another container, random access, global storage, or arithmetic encoding of multiple values. Recursive calls may retain a fixed number of local values each. Return no separate result: reverse the supplied stack. Bottom-to-top input [4,8,1] must become [1,8,4]. Choose a correct method under these restrictions.

options.text: Pop the top, recursively reverse the rest, then insert the saved value at the bottom by recursively removing and restoring the values above that bottom.
options.feedback: Removing the latest value and placing it beneath the reversed remainder produces the reversed order using only allowed stack operations and recursive locals.

options.text: Pop the top, recursively reverse the rest, then push the saved value back on top.
options.feedback: On [4,8,1], this restores every value to its original position and leaves the stack unchanged.

options.text: Pop all values recursively, then push them during recursive unwinding in the order they were popped.
options.feedback: Recursive unwinding exposes the earliest popped values last; pushing each frame local on unwind rebuilds the original [4,8,1] rather than its reverse.

options.text: Drain into an auxiliary array, then access its indices to rebuild the desired order.
options.feedback: An auxiliary array and indexed access violate the explicitly allowed storage and operations, regardless of the resulting order.

feedback.reason: The allowed access is only at the top; recursive bottom insertion trades repeated traversal for using call frames instead of another container.
details: Save the top in a local recursive frame. Reverse the remaining stack, then call a helper that inserts the saved value at the bottom by popping, recursing, and restoring intervening tops. Stop each recursion on an empty stack.

Reversing the remainder is not enough: the removed top must be inserted at its bottom. That helper temporarily removes and restores all intervening values. Time adds over decreasing stack sizes, while peak live frames remain linear.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For recursive-bottom-insertion, choose the tightest worst-case total time and auxiliary-space bounds in terms of n, the input length.
constraints: The supplied stack is mutated in place and excluded from auxiliary space; no separate output exists.
Every push, pop, and empty check costs constant time. Both recursive procedures use fixed-size local values. All live recursive frames count as auxiliary space.
No copying, hashing, encoded values, additional containers or random-access operations are used.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Bottom insertion costs sum quadratically; simultaneously live recursion frames are linear.
details: At size m, inserting at bottom traverses m entries; summing these costs over sizes gives O(n²) time. Reverse and insertion frames together retain O(n) fixed-size locals at peak, not O(n²). The mutated input is excluded, but the call stack counts.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Every restored value must be moved again during later bottom insertions; insertion costs sum across stack sizes.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This misses both repeated bottom insertion work and the linear peak of live recursive frames.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Even one bottom insertion traverses the full stack; the repeated insertions are quadratic overall.

methodReveal.title: Reverse the remainder and insert below it
methodReveal.description: Save the top in a local recursive frame. Reverse the remaining stack, then call a helper that inserts the saved value at the bottom by popping, recursing, and restoring intervening tops. Stop each recursion on an empty stack.
